question: Which crop did the British force the peasants of Assam to produce?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• The British forced the peasants of Assam to produce **tea** because of its high demand in European markets during the colonial period.
 
• **Assam** emerged as one of the primary tea-producing regions in India under British colonial rule, with the establishment of plantations in the 19th century.
 
• The British introduced the **plantation system**, which involved large-scale tea farming and employed laborers, often under exploitative conditions.
 
• The **Tea Act of 1834** was instrumental in the expansion of tea plantations in India, especially in Assam, as British companies monopolized the industry.
 
• Tea plantations in Assam significantly contributed to the **economic exploitation** of Indian resources and labor under British rule.
